findings.description: Activation patching implements necessity test correctly: clean/corrupted paradigm with block-input pre-hook replacement of s at target residues
Donors verified as non-hairpin at corresponding target residue positions in native DSSP — valid corrupted-state source
Predicted direction (early s-patch drops hairpin rate ≥0.2pp) confirmed: Δ=-0.862 in correct direction
Three controls (z-patch, matched-ctrl, late-window) all show <10% of early s-patch effect, ruling out non-selective perturbation artifacts
Family = Causal Attribution / Patching per MECHANISM_ROUTING.md; implementation uses block-input activation patching submethod exactly
Block-specific donor tensors used (one per block k via pre-hook capture); not averaged across blocks
Donor s tensors come from different sequence distribution — intrinsic limitation of activation patching. Mitigated by N=197 random pairings and three specificity controls.
Baseline condition run per chain; baseline_rate=100% confirms hairpin present before intervention
Context manager with handle.remove() ensures no hook leakage across chain iterations
